standard.title: Images extend meaning
standard.description: identify how images extend the meaning of a text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand that images add to or multiply meaning in texts (AC9E2LA08). They have not yet focused on how images extend meaning specifically — adding information or dimensions that the written text alone does not provide.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify how images extend the meaning of a text.

nodes.label: Images add information not in the words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify information that an image provides that is not stated in the accompanying written text.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one piece of information an image adds that is not in the written text, and explain what the image tells the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise how images extend meaning by adding information not in the words — including how the relationship between characters can be depicted through position, expression and gesture that the words don't explicitly describe.
wider: Compare what a text with its images says versus the same text without them — discussing what meaning is lost when the images are removed
Examine how the same event is shown in an image versus described in words, and discuss what each mode does better
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who still treat images as illustrations of what the words say (rather than as extending meaning) lack the analytical stance needed for N2 — gaze, angle and distance analysis requires students to already be reading images as meaning-makers.

response_modes.reason: Students often treat images as illustrations of what the words already say. Multiple examples where the image adds genuinely new information — not just pictures of what is written — helps students see extending as distinct from illustrating.

success_criteria: Student identifies specific information in the image that is not stated in the written text
Student explains what meaning the image adds — not just that 'it shows what's happening'

nodes.label: Images construct relationship with viewer
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how images construct a relationship between the depicted content and the viewer through gaze, angle and distance.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one image feature (e.g. direct gaze, close distance, angle) and explain how it creates a particular relationship or feeling for the viewer.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise how images construct a relationship with the viewer through direct gaze into the camera, social distance and angle — explaining what each choice creates for the viewer.
wider: Compare two images of the same subject using different angles and distances, and discuss how the choices change the viewer's relationship with the subject
Find examples in picture books or media where image choices position the viewer to feel sympathy, distance, or power, and discuss how the technical choices create that effect

response_modes.reason: The connection between technical image choices (gaze, angle, distance) and their effect on the viewer requires explicit reasoning — students need the chain from 'the character is looking at me' to 'this creates a sense of connection/invitation'. The reasoning link doesn't come automatically.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Image-viewer relationship analysis is rich and engaging at Y3 — students can apply these ideas to picture books, advertisements and screen media they already encounter. The analytical vocabulary (gaze, angle, distance) is appropriately accessible and builds visual literacy that extends across media.
success_criteria: Student identifies a specific image feature (gaze, angle or distance)
Student explains what relationship or feeling that feature creates for the viewer
